scenes.line1: Can you rerun your pipeline safely?
scenes.say: When you rerun your ETL pipeline, will it break things or keep data clean? And what happens when you need to fix historical records?

scenes.label: Idempotent
scenes.sub: Running the same job multiple times gives the same result.
scenes.say: Idempotency means running your job again with the same input always produces the same output. No duplicates, no mess.
To be robust, use upserts or merges for idempotency. For backfills, rerun the pipeline on specific dates to fix past errors.

scenes.title: Upsert in Action
scenes.say: Upserts and merge commands help you avoid duplicates when reprocessing data. They keep your tables clean.

scenes.question: What happens if a pipeline isn't idempotent?
scenes.right: Reruns and backfills can create duplicates or corrupt data.
scenes.say: If your pipeline isn't idempotent, reruns or backfills can mess up your data with duplicates or errors. That's a big interview red flag.
